doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Starting in 2000 and the idea for A Great Night in Harlem
summary: Working from a union cubicle with $7,000, she gets $10,000 from Steve Siegel and conceives the Apollo concert after watching A Great Day in Harlem; the first was 13 days after 9/11.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So you come in in 2000, and as I recall from reading your bios and press materials online, your office was a cubicle in the Musicians Union building, and within a fairly short time you realized that you were under-funded. Let me ask you this. Did you come up with an overall strategy for what you wanted to do? Was it more by the seat of your pants, reacting to different needs as they arose? How did you start to develop your m.o. for addressing the organization’s needs?

I think that with everything, when something is needed, you get resourceful and you come up with it. We needed money, I went to one of my original Street News donors, Steve Siegel, who has been amazing, and he gave us $10,000. We had only had $7,000 in the bank. You can’t help a lot of people with that. At the time, I think we were paying the union only $250 a month in rent, which was great. So I wouldn’t call it strategy. But I remember thinking we’ve got to get more money than this. I also was really... I joke and say I was just a train-station bluesman, but I really didn’t know a lot about jazz. I really knew very little. So I went to learn about it. I rented Jean Bach’s Great Day In Harlem, figuring, “at least I’ll know who everyone is.” That’s the night I got the idea for A Great Night In Harlem to do at the Apollo Theater, and we brought jazz and blues back to the Apollo they told us after 50 years... That concert was amazing.

2001, the first one. It was 13 days after 9/11 happened. We didn’t know if anyone would even show up. And people needed the music healing, because the place was packed. We had about 100 of the legends show up.
